subject: Post-demo: deployment options & EU data residency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Anders Johansen <anders.j@nordbank.eu>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: deployment options & EU data residency

Hi Lucie / Anders,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our demo and next steps on deployment mode and data residency: 

- What we heard: NordBank needs EU-only data residency for customer data, low-deterministic latency for customer-facing features, and a clear procurement timeline (Q4 target).
- Deployment options we reviewed: Hosted API (fastest to go-live; we can route requests through our eu-west region but need to validate EU-only ingress for your regulatory team), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools in a customer-isolated tenancy — good middle ground for predictable throughput), Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict regulatory isolation.
- Our recommendation based on the call: Start with a Hosted API pilot for non-critical workloads to validate integration and latency, then evaluate Dedicated or Private for production-sensitive flows. If NordBank requires customer-managed VPC or on-prem isolation from day 1, we should prioritize Private.

Action items:
1) Marissa: Share EU-region architecture overview and SOC2 summary (attached).
2) Lucie: Confirm whether EU-only ingress (no cross-region routing) is a hard requirement or if a Virtual Private Cloud peering / Dedicated option is acceptable.
3) If helpful, I’ll loop in Sean (solutions) to go over network diagrams and timelines for Dedicated vs Private.

Attachments: redwood-eu-deployment-overview.pdf, SOC2-summary.pdf

Available times for a follow-up deep-dive next week: Tue/Wed 10:00–13:00 CET or Thu 14:00–16:00 CET.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182
From: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@nordbank.eu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T17:40:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment options & EU data residency

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our security & infra teams: 

1) EU-only ingress requirement: for some regulated products we cannot allow egress or routing through non-EU regions at any point. Does Redwood offer a Hosted API plan that guarantees EU-only routing and processing (i.e., no fallback to US regions)?
2) If the Hosted option can be restricted to EU-only, what are the controls/audits & SLAs we can show to our auditors?
3) For Dedicated vs Private: can you provide a high-level timeline and rough cost band for standing up Dedicated capacity in our account vs Private VPC deployment? Our procurement timeline is tight so speed to production matters.

We reviewed the attachments — SOC2 summary looks good but our auditors will want network diagrams and architecture notes specific to EU routing. Can Sean join the follow-up to walk through those?

Appreciate it — happy to book Tue 10:30 CET if that works.

Best,
Lucie
Head of Cloud Security | NordBank
lucie.dubois@nordbank.eu

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lucie Dubois <lucie.dubois@nordbank.eu>, Anders Johansen <anders.j@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-31T07:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: deployment options & EU data residency — technical follow-up & diagrams

Lucie / Anders — looping in Sean from Solutions so he can jump into the network/architecture questions. Sean — NordBank is evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; key constraint is EU-only data residency (no cross-region routing) for some product lines. They are targeting a procurement decision in Q4 and want timelines and high-level cost bands.

Quick answers up-front while Sean prepares detail: 
- Hosted API: We operate an EU region (eu-west1). For standard Hosted customers we can route and process requests entirely in the EU region; however, the Hosted offering is multitenant and some control plane operations are global. For customers with a strict EU-only legal requirement we typically recommend Dedicated (single-tenant capacity) or Private (VPC/on-prem) to provide stronger contractual guarantees and network isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: Can be provisioned in an EU region in a reserved pool. Typical lead time is 4–8 weeks after contract signature (depends on capacity and Q4 demand). Cost: mid-to-high range vs Hosted — I can share a ballpark range in the call.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Best for customers requiring customer-managed networking and strong data residency guarantees. Lead time varies (6–12+ weeks) depending on networking, firewall rules, and on-prem provisioning.

Sean — attached is the EU deployment overview we sent previously. Can you prepare: 
1) A simple architecture diagram showing EU-only request flow (no cross-region egress),
2) A checklist of controls we can put into contract (data residency clause, region SLA, audit logs), and
3) A rough timeline/cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private.

Lucie — Tue 10:30 CET works for us. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 20 min architecture/Q&A, 20 min timeline/cost, 10 min next steps.

Attachments: deployment-runbook.xlsx, redwood-eu-deployment-overview.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
